audit.why: Rakan edges level 1, Pyke spikes at 2 off Q+E, Rakan reclaims 3-5 with W-Q peel, Rakan's ult wins level 6, Pyke's first-item hook-reset flips first item, Rakan out-teamfights late — matches packet.levelChart exactly.

audit.whatIsWrong: All 7 phases[N].side were the placeholder 'Skill' while win[0..6] already alternates Rakan/Pyke/Rakan/Rakan/Rakan/Pyke/Rakan, and the why text for several rows didn't state that verdict.
audit.why: The chart token and the prose below it must agree, and each why must actually justify its side.
audit.corrected: Set phases[N].side to match win[N] for all 7 rows and rewrite whys that were still generic.

audit.whatIsWrong: missingInteractions flags that Pyke's Gift of the Drowned Ones (P) bypasses stacked resistances, and Ghostwater Dive (W) camo has no Rakan reveal tool — neither appears anywhere on the page. breakdown.cooldowns also has no real number.
audit.why: Building raw armour/MR into Pyke is a wasted item slot, and without a sweeper/Control Ward his camo engage is invisible until it lands.
audit.corrected: State Bone Skewer is 10-8s, note Pyke ignores stacked resistances for bonus AD instead, and that Ghostwater Dive needs a Control Ward or sweeper to see through.

edits.before: - Pyke Bone Skewer: matchup-defining — The hook starts the chain — his R cleans what it catches. It writes your spacing rules. - E Battle Dance is for saving fights, not seasoning trades. - The R opens or closes fights — pick one per cast.
edits.after: - Bone Skewer is down 10s at rank 1, 8s by rank 5 — his R cleans whatever it catches, so it writes your spacing rules. - He ignores stacked resistances for bonus AD (Gift of the Drowned Ones) — armour/MR alone won't slow him. - Ghostwater Dive camo needs a Control Ward or sweeper; you have no innate reveal.

edits.before: Q the pair for the heal, W the window, E home — the trade paid twice and answered once.
edits.after: Ward the lane bushes — Pyke fishes Bone Skewer from fog, and a Control Ward denies his Ghostwater Dive approach too.

edits.before: Entrancing into a banked disengage — the bird that flies into tornadoes writes the highlight for the other team.
edits.after: Building pure armour/MR into him wastes the slot — his passive converts stacked resistances into bonus AD instead.

edits.before: Q-poke the contacts — the feather heals your carry on connect; the trade pays twice.
edits.after: Better base range control and roam threat let you edge level 1 before his hook is a real threat.

edits.before: W threat begins: the leap governs their spacing from fog already.
edits.after: Bone Skewer paired with Phantom Undertow gives him a hook-into-stun that outranges your W engage at 2.

edits.before: Full kit: E-hop the angles and W the windows — your engage range is two screens of charm.
edits.after: Your W-Q peel cancels his hook attempts by 3, and his high Q mana cost gives you a punishable window.

edits.before: Zone with entrance threat and shield-hop the margins — the bird is everywhere at once.
edits.after: Through 4-5 his Q mana cost keeps punishing him, and your peel timing controls the trade.

edits.before: The Quickness online — the charm drive-by starts fights five people deep.
edits.after: Grand Entrance chains a clean all-in for your ADC, while Death From Below needs a target already low — you win the level-6 ult trade.

edits.before: First item: the knockups chain and the hops multiply.
edits.after: His first roam item revives the hook-stun-reset pick threat and his R resets snowball fast off it.

edits.before: Late Rakan opens everything: R through the formation, W the center, and E home through the panic.
edits.after: Your AoE charm and knockup peel out-teamfight his squishy single-target dives once you're grouped.
